builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI
summary: This architecture replaces single-agent LLM pipelines and text-centric RAG with a three-engine system comprising a financial knowledge graph for provenance and relationships, a deterministic optimization engine for calculations, and a multi-agent LLM layer for orchestration and validation. It costs deployment complexity in building reusable ERP mappings, graph templates, and validation policies, though observed deployment time reduced from roughly six to two weeks once these assets exist. ERP data quality issues and tenant-specific schema variations remain major implementation challenges that can compromise context quality and validation accuracy.
rationale: The architecture is explicitly production-grounded for constrained environments, requires no foundation-model training or cluster infrastructure, and delivers auditable numerical accuracy and traceability that single-agent systems cannot guarantee.
technique: Three-engine architecture with graph-backed multi-agent validation

claims.statement: This architecture replaces single-agent LLM pipelines and text-centric RAG with a three-engine system comprising a financial knowledge graph for provenance and relationships, a deterministic optimization engine for calculations, and a multi-agent LLM layer for orchestration and validation. It costs deployment complexity in building reusable ERP mappings, graph templates, and validation policies, though observed deployment time reduced from roughly six to two weeks once these assets exist. ERP data quality issues and tenant-specific schema variations remain major implementation challenges that can compromise context quality and validation accuracy.
Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed hallucination rates from 7-9% (single-agent) to below 1%, although findings are observational rather than causal.
